intro: Android files, right at home on your Mac.
compatibility: Built for macOS 14+. Tested on macOS 27.2; older versions still need real-device validation. Liquid Glass is available on macOS 26+.
nativeTitle: A familiar place for your files.
nativeBody: Browse folders, search file names, and drag files in. Built with native Mac controls, system colors, and Liquid Glass on supported versions.
progressBody: File counts, overall progress, speed, and time remaining stay in view. If a transfer stops, completed files are preserved and the failed item is reported.
agentBody: The maf CLI shares the same transfer engine. JSON results, stable error codes and a clear USB session status help scripts and agents work reliably.
startTitle: A cable is all you need.
step1: Connect with a USB data cable. Unlock Android and select File Transfer / Android Auto.
step2: Quit other MTP apps. Open MacAndFiles, select your device and connect.
step3: Send to Android or Save to Mac. Folders copy recursively; existing names are never silently overwritten.
cliTitle: The same app. A short command.
cliBody: Install maf from More → Terminal and Agents in the app. If needed, add ~/.local/bin to PATH. Disconnect the GUI before a CLI file operation.
statusBody: The downloadable ZIP is an ad-hoc signed development build. Developer ID signing and Apple notarization are not yet complete. Build locally if you prefer; release status is documented in the repository.

searchQ: Does search look through the whole device?
searchA: Search filters file names in the current folder. It does not scan the entire device or app-private storage.
privacyQ: Do my files go through a cloud service?
privacyA: No. Transfers run locally over USB. There is no account, cloud relay, analytics or advertising in the app or this site.
